commentary:
Energy owns the tape this morning. Brent is pressing toward $100 (+2.4% at 99.32) and WTI is up 3.4% after Houthi strikes halted operations at Saudi energy facilities across four cities, while traders estimate Hormuz flows are running at roughly half pre-war levels; heating oil and RBOB are up 3% and 1.2%, and TTF gained 2.1% in sympathy. That supply shock is landing on a market already fretting sticky inflation — Schwab notes last week's hot jobs report lifted Fed rate-hike odds, and Bloomberg's wrap frames the equity slide squarely as oil-driven inflation jitters.

The result is classic stagflationary risk-off: S&P and Dow futures lower (the Dow also dented by a Swiss pharma trial setback hammering the SMI, -1.7%), Treasuries sold at the long end with the US Long Bond -0.4%, Bunds and Gilts softer, and gold -0.9% as higher-for-longer real rates trump the geopolitical bid. Elsewhere the yen rallied 1.4% to a seven-month high on safe-haven flows and reports a key adviser in Tokyo projects a September BoJ hike — pressuring the dollar into this week's US CPI.

China's August trade held up (exports +25% y/y, imports slightly light), supporting copper (+1.3%) and iron ore. In ags, wheat ripped 3% as Russian strikes on Kyiv resumed, reviving Black Sea supply risk, and sugar extended its supply-driven run. Watch: US CPI, further Gulf escalation headlines, and whether crude closes through $100 — that's the number that forces the rates repricing wider.
